# git-cliff changelog — implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use
> superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans
> to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Ship a checked-in `CHANGELOG.md` generated by git-cliff, whose newest section
is also the GitHub Release body.

**Architecture:** `cliff.toml` at repo root drives generation. One-time full backfill
over `v0.1.0a1..a5`, then `--prepend` forever so hand edits survive. The release body is
sliced out of the merged file, never out of cliff's stdout. Runs locally inside the
existing `/release` gates — no CI, no bot.

**Tech stack:** git-cliff 2.13.1 (PyPI wheel, `dev` dependency group), Tera templates,
`gh release create --notes-file`.

Spec:
[`docs/specs/2026-08-10-git-cliff-changelog-design.md`](../specs/2026-08-10-git-cliff-changelog-design.md).

## Global constraints

- Dev deps hard-pinned exact (`git-cliff==2.13.1`), `dependency-groups.dev`, kept sorted
  by the `uv-sort` pre-commit hook.
- `uv run pre-commit run --all-files` is the gate. Prettier owns Markdown
  (`proseWrap = "always"`, `printWidth = 88`) — it reflows `CHANGELOG.md` on every
  commit. Never hand-wrap; let the hook do it. `git add` before running, untracked files
  are skipped.
- No new CI workflow. No changelog page on the docs site.
- Never `git commit --amend`. New commits only. Stay local — no push, no PR, until
  asked.
- Conventional Commit titles on every commit here.

**No automated test surface.** This is config + generated Markdown; there is no pytest
target and adding one is out of scope. Every task's gate is a command whose output gets
read against stated criteria. Do not claim a task passed without pasting the output.

## File map

- `cliff.toml` — create. Commit parsers, tag pattern, Tera body template, GitHub remote
  for compare links.
- `pyproject.toml` — modify. `git-cliff==2.13.1` in `dependency-groups.dev`;
  `CHANGELOG.md` added to `[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist].include`.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — create. Generated, then hand-corrected for `a1..a5`.
- `.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md` — modify. Changelog step + notes slicing, replacing
  the current "summarize what changed" step.
- `uv.lock` — regenerated by `uv sync`.

---

### Task 1: Pin git-cliff

**Files:** modify `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Add the pin**

Add `"git-cliff==2.13.1"` to `[dependency-groups].dev`, alphabetical position.

- [ ] **Step 2: Sync**

Run: `uv sync` Expected: resolves, installs a `git_cliff` wheel matching the venv's
platform.

- [ ] **Step 3: Verify the binary runs**

Run: `uv run git-cliff --version` Expected: `git-cliff 2.13.1`. A `Bad CPU type` /
exec-format error means the venv's Python is Intel-under-Rosetta and picked a mismatched
wheel — stop and report, do not work around it.

- [ ] **Step 4: Commit**

```bash
git add pyproject.toml uv.lock
git commit -m "chore(deps): add git-cliff for changelog generation"
```

---

### Task 2: Write cliff.toml

**Files:** create `cliff.toml`.

**Produces:** the config every later task invokes. Section names below are load-bearing
— Task 4 sorts hand-written entries into exactly these.

**Config requirements** (prose; write the TOML yourself, do not copy a vendor sample
wholesale):

- `[git]`: conventional commits on; unconventional commits filtered out; `v[0-9]*` tag
  pattern so all five alphas are picked up; newest-first ordering within a release.
- `[remote.github]`: `lincolnloop` / `django-absurd`, so release headings can carry a
  `compare/<prev>...<this>` link.
- Commit parsers, kept sections: `feat` → **Features**, `fix` → **Bug fixes**, `perf` →
  **Performance**, `docs` → **Documentation**, `build` → **Requirements**.
- Commit parsers, skipped: `chore` (all of it, including every `chore(deps)`), `ci`,
  `test`, `style`, `refactor`.
- **Breaking changes** is a template-level section, not a parser — git-cliff already
  sets `commit.breaking` from the `!` marker and the `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer. Render
  it first, above Features, and do not also emit those commits under their own type.
- Subjects already end in `(#N)` from squash-merge. Turn that into a PR link
  (`link_parsers`, or template-side) rather than duplicating the number.
- Header explains the file is generated by git-cliff and hand-edited at release time.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write `cliff.toml` to the above**

- [ ] **Step 2: Render the unreleased range and read it**

Run: `uv run git-cliff --unreleased --tag v0.1.0a6` Expected, against `v0.1.0a5..HEAD`:

- `feat!: regenerate the schema as a single 0.5.0 install (#169)` and
  `feat(pg_cron)!: validate schedule grammar in Python…(#163)` under **Breaking
  changes**, and NOT repeated under Features.
- `feat!: one worker mode, with working concurrency (#156)` under Breaking changes.
- `feat: log steps, replays, sleeps and event waits (#154)` under **Features**.
- `docs: rewrite the documentation site as an example-first how-to (#161)` under
  **Documentation**.
- Zero lines mentioning pre-commit hooks, `renovatebot/`, `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv`,
  `actions/checkout`, or lock file maintenance.
- Every `(#N)` resolves to `https://github.com/lincolnloop/django-absurd/pull/N`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Render the full history and confirm five releases exist**

Run: `uv run git-cliff | grep -E '^## '`

Expected, and verified during implementation: **three** headings, not five. `v0.1.0a2`,
`a3` and `a4` contain only pre-convention prose subjects plus `ci:`/`chore(deps):`, so
their commit lists are empty after filtering and git-cliff omits the release entirely.
This is not a `tag_pattern` fault — all five tags are detected, and `render_always` does
not change it. Task 4 creates those three sections from scratch.

- [ ] **Step 4: Commit**

```bash
git add cliff.toml
git commit -m "chore: configure git-cliff"
```

---

### Task 3: Backfill CHANGELOG.md

**Files:** create `CHANGELOG.md`; modify `pyproject.toml`.

This is the ONLY task that may use `-o`. Every later write is `--prepend`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Generate**

Run: `uv run git-cliff -o CHANGELOG.md`

- [ ] **Step 2: Ship it in the sdist**

Add `"CHANGELOG.md"` to `[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist].include` — the allowlist is
explicit, so a new root file is invisible to the sdist otherwise.

- [ ] **Step 3: Format and commit**

```bash
git add CHANGELOG.md pyproject.toml
uv run pre-commit run --all-files
git add CHANGELOG.md
git commit -m "docs: generate the changelog for v0.1.0a1..a5"
```

Prettier reflows the file on first run; re-add and commit the reflowed version. Commit
the raw generated state before Task 4 so the hand corrections are reviewable as their
own diff.

---

### Task 4: Correct the pre-conventional releases

**Files:** modify `CHANGELOG.md`.

Conventional titles only became mandatory around `#131`, so most of `a1..a4` is prose
that Task 2's config drops on the floor.

**`v0.1.0a2`, `a3` and `a4` have no section at all** — git-cliff omits a release whose
filtered commit list is empty. Write those three headings yourself, in the same format
the generated ones use (heading text, date, compare link), in the correct position in
the file. `a3` and `a4` carry real user-visible work — the native-async worker,
auto-created queues — that no generator can recover.

Also fix the one `upper_first` artifact: `feat(test): dj_absurd fixture…` renders as
`Dj_absurd fixture…`.

- [ ] **Step 1: List what was dropped, per release**

```bash
for range in v0.1.0a1..v0.1.0a2 v0.1.0a2..v0.1.0a3 v0.1.0a3..v0.1.0a4 v0.1.0a4..v0.1.0a5; do
  echo "== $range"
  git log --format='%s' "$range" | grep -vE '^(feat|fix|perf|docs|build|chore|ci|test|style|refactor)(\(.+\))?!?:'
done
```

Also list what `v0.1.0a1` itself contains: `git log --format='%s' v0.1.0a1`.

- [ ] **Step 2: Read the curated source material**

```bash
for t in v0.1.0a1 v0.1.0a2 v0.1.0a3 v0.1.0a4 v0.1.0a5; do gh release view "$t"; done
```

The GitHub notes are better than any commit subject — they are the authority for what
each release meant.

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the entries**

Into the existing generated sections, in the existing entry style, keeping each entry's
`(#N)` link. Rules:

- Drop Renovate/CI/tooling work entirely, same as the config does — a hand-written entry
  is held to the same bar, not a loophole.
- User-visible behaviour only. `Events`, `Cleanup & retention`, `Durable Steps + Sleep`
  are Features. `Rename managed pg_cron job prefix absurd…`,
  `Enforce a single Absurd backend; drop the schedule alias (#77)` and
  `Derive scheduler from pg_cron app presence; drop SCHEDULER/E008 (#81)` are Breaking
  changes — `a5`'s "Upgrade notes" names all three.
- Rewrite subjects into sentences that read like the kept `feat:` entries, not raw log
  lines.
- Commits with no user-visible effect (`Typing fidelity sweep`,
  `Code and docs hygiene sweep (#100)`) get no entry.

- [ ] **Step 4: Verify nothing prose-shaped survived**

Reread each of the five sections. Criteria: no empty release section; no entry that is a
verbatim non-conventional git subject; no tooling entry.

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add CHANGELOG.md
uv run pre-commit run --all-files
git add CHANGELOG.md
git commit -m "docs: fill in the pre-conventional releases by hand"
```

---

### Task 5: Wire the changelog into the release skill

**Files:** modify `.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md`.

**Consumes:** `cliff.toml` from Task 2, `CHANGELOG.md` from Tasks 3–4.

- [ ] **Step 1: Prove the slice command works before documenting it**

The release body is the top section of the merged file — from the first `## [` heading
up to (not including) the second. Work out the command, then run it against the real
`CHANGELOG.md` and read the output.

Criteria: exactly one release's content, its heading included, no bleed from the next
release, no trailing link-reference block.

- [ ] **Step 2: Replace the skill's step 2**

Current step 2 is "Summarize what changed since the last tag" via `git log --oneline`.
Replace with `uv run git-cliff --unreleased` — it is the same information already
grouped by section, and it is the input to the GATE 1 version decision.

- [ ] **Step 3: Add the changelog step between GATE 1 and GATE 2**

Documented as: branch from up-to-date `origin/main`;
`uv run git-cliff --unreleased --tag <version> --prepend CHANGELOG.md` (the tag does not
exist yet — `--tag` supplies the heading); `uv run pre-commit run --all-files`; commit,
PR, merge. State plainly that this PR is where hand-written prose (Highlights, Upgrade
notes) belongs, and that it flows into the release body for free.

- [ ] **Step 4: Rewrite GATE 2 and the create step**

GATE 2 shows the sliced notes file. `gh release create` switches from `--generate-notes`
to `--notes-file`. Add the invariant: **never** `git cliff -o` after the backfill — it
destroys every hand edit.

- [ ] **Step 5: Verify the skill reads as one coherent flow**

Reread start to finish. Criteria: three gates still intact and in order; no leftover
reference to `--generate-notes` or to hand-writing notes directly in the GitHub UI; the
slice command is the one proven in Step 1, verbatim.

- [ ] **Step 6: Record the floor-change convention in `CLAUDE.md`**

The changelog drops `chore(deps)` wholesale, so a floor raise titled that way vanishes.
Add a short rule under the maintenance conventions: raising a supported floor (`Django`,
`absurd-sdk`, `croniter`, Python) is user-visible — title it `feat` or `feat!` with the
floor named in the subject, never `chore(deps)`. Note that `build` is kept as a
**Requirements** section as the safety net, and that Renovate cannot emit `build`
because `renovate.json` pins `semanticCommitType` to `chore`.

- [ ] **Step 7: Commit**

```bash
git add .claude/skills/release/SKILL.md CLAUDE.md
git commit -m "docs: cut releases from the changelog"
```

---

### Task 6: Whole-repo gate

- [ ] **Step 1: Run the hooks clean**

Run: `uv run pre-commit run --all-files` Expected: all pass, no files modified. A
modification means a formatting round is outstanding — commit it.

- [ ] **Step 2: Confirm the sdist carries the changelog**

Run: `uv build --sdist && tar -tzf dist/*.tar.gz | grep CHANGELOG` Expected: one match.
Then `rm -rf dist`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Confirm the backfill is reproducible**

Regenerating must not be needed, but the config must still render:
`uv run git-cliff --unreleased` exits 0 and prints nothing surprising for an empty
range.

No test suite run — nothing in `django_absurd/` or `tests/` changed. Say so rather than
running one.

- [ ] **Step 4: Report**

Summarize the diff versus `origin/main` for maintainer review. Do not push, do not open
a PR.
